fault_sites.description: Attention KV-cache allocation on worker startup
fault_sites.ownership_rule: Rust owns allocation; Objective-C receives an opaque handle and must not free it

fault_sites.description: KV-cache ownership transfer across the FFI boundary on generate_start
fault_sites.ownership_rule: Transfer is atomic: the Rust side drops its reference before the Objective-C side assumes it

fault_sites.description: Cleanup after a partial model-cache initialization failure
fault_sites.ownership_rule: The allocating side releases every sub-allocation; the receiver never sees a partially initialized object

fault_sites.description: Resident generation state (KV-cache, LFM2 conv rolling cache, constraint automaton) across quanta
fault_sites.ownership_rule: Worker owns resident state between authorized quanta; module owns the permit and destroys state on cleanup

fault_sites.description: Acknowledged cancellation cleanup before worker timeout
fault_sites.ownership_rule: Clean cancellation consumes no crash budget; resident state is destroyed and the worker returns no authoritative text

fault_sites.description: Timeout cleanup and worker kill after failed cancellation
fault_sites.ownership_rule: Timeout cleanup charges one crash-budget strike and destroys all resident state
The Rust side drops the loaded-model reference; the Objective-C side releases Metal resources it allocated

fault_sites.description: Supervised worker shutdown and transport session close
fault_sites.ownership_rule: The module closes the transport session; the worker drains in-flight command buffers before exit

fault_sites.description: LFM2 short-convolution rolling cache ownership across the FFI boundary
fault_sites.ownership_rule: The Rust side allocates the fixed-size conv cache; the Objective-C side reads and updates it in place and never frees it

fault_sites.description: LFM2 hybrid step native context teardown when weight preparation fails after the context was created
fault_sites.ownership_rule: The Rust engine struct owns the native context release exclusively through Drop; the prepare-failure error path must not release the context itself
